title: Lecture-only quiz
description: 20 questions built only from what Dr. Zheng covered in class (weeks 1-4), written in the lecture's framing and vocabulary: the combined public ledger, the consensus committee of miners, the two checks before accepting a transaction, fee = inputs - outputs and the zero tip, TXID = double SHA-256, the 10,000-byte transaction limit, Koblitz curve and twin signatures, Chaum's e-cash. Spread is 4/6/3/4/3 rather than 4 per chapter because week 4 is transaction-heavy (chapter 2) while the lecture barely touched Bitcoin Core (chapter 3) and never reached HD wallets (chapter 5).

title: Lecture + book quiz (primary prediction)
description: 20 questions grounded in lecture content AND the corresponding book material (coverage lecture+book), 4 per chapter. This is the primary prediction: the Canvas quiz is a reading quiz on chapters 1-5, and the concepts the instructor also spent class time on are the ones most likely to be asked; every item also lands in a top-8 externally tested theme (internal/research/external-themes.json), so lecture emphasis and community practice agree. Chapter 5's four items lean on the lecture's one wallet idea (a fresh random key per payment) because the lecture never reached HD wallets; see the book quiz for BIP32/39/44 depth.

title: Book-only quiz
description: 20 questions drawn entirely from Mastering Bitcoin chapters 1-5, 4 per chapter, emphasizing material the lecture did not reach and the concepts that recur most in public Mastering Bitcoin practice material (internal/research/external-themes.json): the four innovations, halving toward 21 million, the Byzantine Generals' Problem, address reuse and privacy, mining's two purposes and the coinbase-style reward transaction, six confirmations, the genesis block, Bitcoin Core as the reference implementation, BIPs, pruning, JSON-RPC and bitcoin-cli, HASH160, address prefixes (3, bc1q, bc1p), compressed public keys, HD wallets (BIP32), 12-word codes (BIP39), xprv vs xpub, hardened derivation.
